skill.name: longbridge-technical
skill.description: Provides technical analysis workflows for Longbridge market data, including candlesticks, Ichimoku, indicators, harmonic patterns, Elliott Wave, Chan Theory, SMC, and Turtle signals.
skill.summary: Analyze Longbridge market data with technical frameworks, signal rules, and multilingual reporting guidance.
skill.author: longbridge

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from markdown formatting, finance terminology, math examples, and readable multilingual text. Confirmed findings are limited to intentional local command execution and package-install guidance in SKILL.md. The Turtle workflow also handles sensitive account data, so agents must require explicit user consent before account reads.

remediation.issue: Local CLI execution is part of the workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running longbridge commands, validate symbol formats, and show the exact command before execution.

remediation.issue: Python package installation is recommended for optional methods.
remediation.suggestion: Move pip install steps to setup documentation and ask for user approval before installing czsc, smartmoneyconcepts, pandas, or numpy.

remediation.issue: Turtle workflows may access assets, positions, watchlists, and order history.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for explicit consent before account-data commands, provide manual-input alternatives, and avoid displaying unnecessary balances or order details.

remediation.issue: Temporary file examples use predictable /tmp paths.
remediation.suggestion: Use unique per-session temporary filenames, restrict permissions where possible, and delete intermediate market-data files after analysis.

content.user_title: Analyze Markets with Longbridge Technical Signals
content.value_statement: Traders need consistent technical analysis across many frameworks. This skill applies Longbridge market data to patterns, indicators, wave counts, and Turtle signal workflows.
actual_capabilities: Uses Longbridge K-line data as the required input for OHLCV-based analysis.
Explains candlestick, Ichimoku, RSI, MACD, EMA, Bollinger, KDJ, and volume signals.
Supports harmonic patterns, Elliott Wave counts, Chan Theory structures, and Smart Money Concepts.
Calculates Turtle Trading breakouts, ATR N values, unit sizing, stops, and add-on levels.
Provides output rules for English, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese.
Includes error-handling guidance for missing data, invalid symbols, and unavailable CLI tools.
limitations: Requires reliable OHLCV data from Longbridge or a compatible MCP tool.
May request account values or positions for Turtle sizing, and should only do so with user consent.
Does not execute trades or guarantee investment outcomes.
Some advanced Elliott Wave workflows reference a local script that is not included in the file tree.

use_cases.title: Daily Technical Brief
use_cases.description: Review one symbol with indicators, trend context, and clear caveats before market planning.

use_cases.title: Framework Comparison
use_cases.description: Compare signals from candlestick, Ichimoku, Bollinger, and momentum methods for the same market.

use_cases.title: Turtle Signal Education
use_cases.description: Explain breakout rules, ATR sizing, stop levels, and add-on logic in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze One Symbol
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze AAPL.US with Longbridge technical analysis. Use daily data and explain the main trend, momentum, support, resistance, and risk caveats.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Indicator Signals
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Ichimoku, RSI, MACD, Bollinger Bands, and volume signals for 700.HK. Explain where the frameworks agree or conflict.

prompt_templates.title: Review Turtle Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Check TSLA.US for Turtle Trading signals. Calculate N value, breakout status, stop level, and unit sizing only after asking before any account-data access.

prompt_templates.title: Build Wave Timing Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Elliott Wave timing report for MSFT.US. Include alternate counts, momentum confirmation, market context, invalidation levels, and stock-specific caveats.

output_examples.output: The response identifies cloud position, baseline support, RSI condition, momentum alignment, and clear caveats about data quality and risk.

output_examples.input: Scan my watchlist for Turtle signals.
output_examples.output: The response asks before reading the watchlist, then summarizes breakout candidates, ATR levels, stops, and unsupported symbols.

output_examples.input: Is AAPL.US in a late Elliott Wave impulse?
output_examples.output: The response compares wave counts, checks momentum divergence, states whether the structure is confirmed, and avoids forced conclusions when counts conflict.

best_practices: Confirm the exact Longbridge symbol and market suffix before analysis.
Ask for consent before running commands that access account assets, positions, orders, or watchlists.
Treat every output as technical analysis, not financial advice or a trade instruction.
anti_patterns: Do not install Python packages or Longbridge tools without explicit approval.
Do not read positions, orders, assets, or watchlists unless the user clearly authorizes it.
Do not force a bullish or bearish label when data is incomplete or frameworks disagree.

faq.question: Does this skill place trades?
faq.answer: No. It provides analysis, signal explanations, and risk context only.

faq.question: What data source does it use?
faq.answer: It expects Longbridge K-line and quote data, or an equivalent Longbridge MCP data source.

faq.question: Does it require account login?
faq.answer: Most technical analysis does not. Turtle sizing may need account values or positions, which require user consent.

faq.question: Which languages are supported?
faq.answer: The skill includes guidance for English, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese responses.

faq.question: Are optional dependencies required?
faq.answer: Some Chan Theory, SMC, and Elliott Wave workflows may need optional Python packages or local scripts.

faq.question: Is this financial advice?
faq.answer: No. Outputs should include caveats and should not promise returns or give guaranteed buy or sell conclusions.
